points: Yirmiyahu's repeated metaphor: the Jewish people are an unfaithful wife, and brazenly so. By law she couldn't go back, yet Hashem says, I want you back.
Yehudah is worse than the ten tribes, because they saw what happened to the north and didn't learn from it.
Rashi says Yirmiyahu actually went to bring back the ten tribes, a hundred years after their exile and after centuries of hostility.

Rabbi Binyamin Lau shows his tact: he doesn't mention Yerushalayim or Dovid's line, and even says the Aron won't matter so much. Peace comes through sensitivity, not proving you were right. Many came back.

"Shuvu banim shovavim": Elisha ben Avuyah heard "except for Acher" and thought he was rejected. But it meant leave the bad part behind. He saw his flaws as his identity; our true self is a pure neshamah.
